expectations.text: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
expectations.evidence: Open Questions (Q-###) and Assumptions (ASM-###) plus a companion notes file with grounded defects D1-D8.

expectations.text: Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Summary, Problem Statement, Non-Goals, Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, verification, and Open Questions present.

expectations.text: Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
expectations.evidence: Uses REQ-###, AC-###, NFR-###, ASM-###, Q-### conventions.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
expectations.evidence: Every AC is checkable by inspecting the edited skill files or running the evals; definition of done ties REQ to passing AC.

expectations.text: Grounds the spec in the current `defining-specifications` skill content based on read-only inspection.
expectations.evidence: Source Context cites SKILL.md v1.2, both references, and evals.json; Problem Statement enumerates specific defects (DEC-### orphan, Status lifecycle) found by inspection.

expectations.text: Keeps tickets, task decomposition, and implementation edits explicitly out of scope.
expectations.evidence: For Implementing Agents and Non-Goals exclude tickets, task decomposition, branches, commits, PRs.

expectations.text: Functional requirements are written in EARS form, using 'shall' with When/If/While/Where keywords where appropriate.
expectations.evidence: Requirements use 'shall' with EARS keywords (confirmed by the skill's agent-handoff profile being applied).

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria use Given/When/Then phrasing and reference the requirement IDs they verify (traceability).
expectations.evidence: ACs use Given/When/Then and name the REQ-### they verify; a REQ->AC->TEST traceability matrix is included.

expectations.text: Includes a 'For Implementing Agents' handoff orientation that identifies authoritative sections and treats open questions as blockers rather than guessing.
expectations.evidence: 'For Implementing Agents' block names authoritative sections and states 'Open Questions (Q-###) are blockers, not decisions.'
